target_customer: Cancer centers, community oncology practices and life sciences sponsors
problem: Oncology staff manually read unstructured records (pathology, notes, genomics, faxes) to match patients to trials, prepare visits and report quality data, which is slow and costly.
business_model: Enterprise B2B software sold to health systems and life sciences firms
product_category: Healthcare AI agents and LLMs for oncology EHR data (OncoLLM)

founders.name: Sarim Khan
founders.background_notes: Described by TechCrunch (2024-05) as a former MIT biotech researcher; YC page says chemical engineer with research in tissue engineering and neuroscience. Degree and school not stated.

founders.name: Hrituraj Singh
founders.background_notes: Researcher on language models and reinforcement learning at Adobe Research (YC page); friends with Khan since college (TechCrunch).

founders.name: Sajjan Rajpurohit
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on Lightspeed's profile, surfaced by search; not on the YC page and background not found.

competitors.name: Deep 6 AI
competitors.what: NLP software matching patients to clinical trials using structured and unstructured health data
competitors.traction_then: Providers and trial sponsors network; later acquired by Tempus (2025)
competitors.funding_then: 17M Series A led by Point72 Ventures in November 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting reliable structured facts from messy oncology records at scale needs domain-trained language models, EHR integration and clinical accuracy that was hard for a small team in 2021.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital integrations (Epic marketplace listing claimed), validated models and accumulated oncology data raise switching costs, but large language models and larger vendors lower the technical barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Tempus bought rival Deep 6 AI in 2025; TechCrunch 2026 names scribes Abridge and Nuance as competing on chart summarization. Triomics remained independent and raised a Series B in May 2026.

market_need_then: Cancer centers rely on trained staff to read unstructured charts for trial matching and registry work; TechCrunch (2024) says six centers were using or piloting the product by May 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses triomics.com, an exact .com; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical, evidence-heavy with accuracy and time-saved claims

branding.brand_signature: OncoLLM and PRISM product names tied to oncology

brand_strength.rationale: Credible clinical positioning with named customers such as Memorial Sloan Kettering, but no evidence that the name or identity itself drove adoption.

pivots.to: Broader oncology AI agents (visit prep, registry abstraction, quality reporting) built on OncoLLM
pivots.why: TechCrunch says founders saw LLMs could extract EHR data; expansion happened as LLM capability grew. Year approximate and not stated by a source.

outcome_analysis: Triomics grew from a trial matching idea into oncology AI agents as language models matured, winning named cancer centers (MSK deployment announced November 2025) and raising a 15M Series A in May 2024 and a 22M Series B in May 2026. The LLM timing tailwind and enterprise hospital sales drove growth; it is active and independent.
notes: Series B is also reported by HLTH, Healthcare IT Today and Goodwin, each citing Battery Ventures as lead and total funding over 36M; announcement day varies (May 27 or 28, 2026). TechCrunch 2024 does not say who led the Series A. Seed amount not found and not recorded; earlier funding may exist. Founding year 2021 per TechCrunch although the batch is Winter 2021 and some databases say 2020. Deep 6 AI is dated to its 2019 round; other competitors (QuantHealth, Trialjectory) are named in 2024 coverage only and not added. The 2023 pivot date is an approximation.
